source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lewisville DFW2 publishes 12 MW of IT capacity, which is 2.5 percent of Texas's 475 MW of published data center load and ranks 12th among the 19 Texas sites that report a capacity figure.

Texas has 133 mapped data center sites, and only 19 of them publish a capacity number. Any state ranking therefore rests on a small minority of the actual footprint, and the 475 MW total is a sum of what operators chose to disclose rather than a measure of what is built. At this campus, 12 MW spread across 200,000 square feet of technical space works out to roughly 300 racks at 40 kW per rack, the density typical of AI training. That is a small hall by current AI standards.

The certifications listed, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, point to regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government rather than to AI training. A 12 MW facility can host AI compute, but it is not sized to anchor a frontier training cluster. The suitability score of 58 is derived from published IT capacity and operator type, and the one input named as missing is announced expansion.

Nothing in the published specifications establishes grid headroom in the Dallas-Fort Worth region, which is the constraint that would decide whether the campus can grow. The data covers disclosed specs only, so it cannot distinguish a finished facility from one with room to expand. No expansion announcements, coordinates, or interconnection figures are included.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
